beats.say: Start with points one comma one, two comma two and three comma three. Their mean is two comma two. Subtract that same mean from every row: the centered points are minus one comma minus one, zero comma zero, and one comma one. Project onto the unit direction one comma one divided by the square root of two. The coordinates become minus square root of two, zero and positive square root of two.

For an N by d centered data matrix, thin singular value decomposition writes X as U Sigma V transpose. With r equal to the smaller of N and d, U is N by r and V is d by r. Centering limits rank to at most the smaller of N minus one and d. The leading columns of V give the retained directions. Covariance eigenvalues are the squared singular values divided by N minus one when N exceeds one. Explained variance retained is the retained sum of squared singular values divided by the total.

Forming X transpose X squares the matrix condition number and can worsen numerical sensitivity; direct SVD avoids that explicit product. Some PCA solvers use covariance, so record the actual solver. PCA centers features without automatically standardizing them. Scaling and whitening change the geometry and need their own validation. Fit supervised preprocessing inside each training fold; select dimensions on development queries and reserve fresh test queries.

A random projection draws one matrix and reuses it for every document and query. A Gaussian construction uses entries with mean zero and variance one over the output dimension. A sparse Achlioptas construction uses positive and negative square root of three over k with probability one sixth each, and zero with probability two thirds. Save the matrix or a reproducible generation contract; do not draw a new space per request.

A Johnson-Lindenstrauss existence bound for a fixed set of N points uses k at least four natural log N divided by the quantity epsilon squared over two minus epsilon cubed over three, for epsilon between zero and one. It bounds squared Euclidean distortion between one minus epsilon and one plus epsilon. This conservative sufficient bound can exceed the original dimension: ten million points at epsilon point one five require about six thousand three hundred sixty-eight dimensions. It is not a useful compression promise for fifteen thirty-six dimensions, nor a statement that every arbitrary draw succeeds.

The guarantee concerns a fixed point set, not automatically future queries or rankings. Two nearby distances can have overlapping allowed intervals and exchange order. For epsilon point one five, a squared-distance bound corresponds to ordinary-distance changes of about minus seven point eight to plus seven point two percent. In the actual seeded forty-eight to sixteen worksheet, raw float bytes fall from one hundred ninety-two to sixty-four, while original-neighbor overlap at five is only point three one seven. Normalize and evaluate the actual cosine pipeline if that is the serving metric.

Dimension reduction changes the coordinate count. Quantization changes the bits used for those coordinates. Our symmetric scalar teaching codec uses integers from minus one hundred twenty-seven through one hundred twenty-seven. Fit a scale of one hundred twenty-seven divided by the document calibration maximum absolute value. Multiply, round and clip, then divide by that scale to reconstruct. Reuse calibration for queries, and account for scale metadata and clipping; this is not a claim about every vendor codec.

Binary sign coding writes one for a positive coordinate and zero otherwise, then compares codes with XOR and population count. It loses magnitudes: equal signs can hide quite different cosines. Two hundred fifty-six float32 coordinates need one thousand twenty-four bytes, scalar eight-bit codes need two hundred fifty-six, and packed sign bits need thirty-two, before metadata. The executed small arrays demonstrate these byte counts and Hamming distances rather than establishing semantic recall.

Current Qdrant documentation separates codec choice, oversampling and full-vector rescoring. For an explicitly requested limit of one hundred and oversampling two point four, select two hundred forty candidates before rescoring. A candidate omitted from that shortlist cannot return. Version one point eighteen introduced TurboQuant; its random rotation preserves distances before lossy coding, not after arbitrary rounding. Pin the server version, bits and rescore settings. Compression ratio alone does not establish a matching latency improvement.

Product quantization splits a vector into m disjoint blocks, trains a centroid codebook per block and stores a centroid identifier for each block. With two hundred fifty-six centroids, each identifier fits one byte. A one hundred twenty-eight-coordinate float32 vector uses five hundred twelve bytes; eight block identifiers use eight bytes, a sixty-four-fold raw-code reduction. Shared codebooks and the index remain additional storage. Each centroid has its block’s coordinate width. Across all m codebooks there are m times K times d over m coordinates, which equals K times d; multiply by the bytes per float for shared codebook storage.

Asymmetric distance computation keeps the query unquantized. For every block and centroid, build a table containing the squared Euclidean distance from that query block to the centroid. A stored code selects one table entry per block; sum them. With ninety-six blocks and two hundred fifty-six centroids, float32 tables use ninety-six kibibytes per query. Whether those tables fit a relevant cache and whether table construction is worthwhile depend on the hardware and workload.

Symmetric computation also quantizes the query, adding query approximation without a universal factor-of-two error rule. Squared distance to reconstructed PQ vectors does not automatically equal cosine distance between unit vectors. The executed forty-row toy uses two one-byte identifiers with four centroids each: sixteen raw float bytes become two code bytes, plus a sixty-four-byte shared codebook. Four centroids could be bit-packed further; this worksheet deliberately stores byte identifiers. Train only on the allowed corpus and test the entire metric pipeline.

Compare judged recall, critical slices, index bytes, build time, latency and cost on the same evaluation protocol. Invalid or nonfinite metrics, missing fields and nonpositive or noninteger byte counts must fail before threshold comparisons.

The article’s authored deployment table requires Recall at ten at least point nine seven five and at most twelve hundred bytes per vector. Full vectors use six thousand one hundred forty-four bytes at recall one. Native shortening uses one thousand twenty-four bytes at point nine eight four; PCA the same bytes at point nine seven one; PQ sixteen bytes at point nine three nine. Only the native candidate meets both worksheet gates. These table values are supplied scenarios, not fresh provider benchmarks.

Supported shortening from fifteen thirty-six float coordinates to two hundred fifty-six, followed by eight-bit coding, changes six thousand one hundred forty-four raw bytes to two hundred fifty-six, a factor of twenty-four. It does not promise a twenty-four-fold total index or latency reduction, nor a cheaper encoder forward pass. Keep any full-vector rescore store in the total.
